descripcion: The past simple tells the main events of a story; the past continuous sets the background or an action interrupted by another. At B1 the goal is to combine both correctly: I was walking home when it started to rain.

filas: I was cooking when the phone rang.
While I was cooking, she was setting the table.

ejemplos.texto: I was walking home when it started to rain.
While I was cooking, she was setting the table.
I called her yesterday, but she didn't answer.

notas: When usually introduces the interrupting event (past simple); while introduces the background action (past continuous).
The past continuous is formed with was/were + -ing.
Not every past story needs the past continuous — use it only for background or interruption.

contraste.es: Spanish uses the imperfecto for the background of a story (estaba cocinando) and the indefinido for the main event (sonó el teléfono), with a logic very close to English. The transfer is generally direct.
contraste.de: German has no continuous form and uses the Präteritum both for the background and for the main event (Als das Telefon klingelte, kochte ich). German speakers therefore under-use the past continuous and write When the phone rang, I cooked, which in English means that the cooking started after the call.
contraste.it: Italian has a very close equivalent: stavo cucinando (I was cooking) for the background and the passato prossimo for the main event. The transfer is usually direct; the one risk is the imperfetto for habits (andavo a scuola a piedi), which leads to I was going to school on foot instead of I used to go.
contraste.fr: The French imparfait covers the background (je cuisinais quand le téléphone a sonné), which maps well onto the past continuous. The imparfait is also used for habits (j'allais à l'école à pied), which leads to I was going to school on foot where English uses I used to go.
contraste.pt: Portuguese has a very close equivalent: estava a cozinhar (European) or estava cozinhando (Brazilian) for the background, and the simple past for the main event. The imperfeito for habits (ia a pé para a escola) leads to I was going on foot where English uses I used to go.

errores: Using the past simple for the background action instead of the past continuous.
Using when where while would be more natural, or vice versa.
autochequeo: Is the main event in the past simple?
Is the background action in the past continuous?
Have I used both tenses at least once?
Does the story sound natural, not translated?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on past simple versus past continuous. Check whether the main event and the background action use the correct tense. Do not rewrite the text.
